name: Tree Incidence Parities Produce Nested Maximum Sequences
statement: For a rooted tree $T=(V,E)$ with $n$ edges, put $d_v(x)=\bigoplus_{e\ni v}x_e$ for nonroot vertices, $f(x)=\sum_{v\ne o}d_v(x)$, and $B_s=\{x:f(x)\le s\}$. Then $(B_s)_{s=0}^n$ is a complete maximum sequence with a common nested-coordinate recursion. Up to coordinate reflections, every rank-one maximum class and every rank-$(n-2)$ maximum class on $n\ge2$ coordinates occurs in such a sequence.
proof: The reduced incidence map is a bijection, giving the Sauer cardinalities. Deleting any $s+1$ tested tree edges leaves a rooted quotient in which a suitable boundary-parity assignment forces at least $s+1$ odd nonroot components, proving the VC bound. Splitting at a leaf orders the two restrictions pointwise and recursively removes that leaf, giving the common nested recursion. Single parity supports are root paths, which model every rank-one maximum tree; complementing parity gives the rank-$(n-2)$ case.
